title: Senegal farm activity defaults (diesel, electricity, yield guides)
description: Screening-level diesel (L/ha/yr), grid electricity (kWh/ha/yr), and yield guides for Senegal farms when the Equipment & Energy step has no measured fuel/electricity. Keyed by mechanization x irrigated, same schema as ghana_farm_activity_defaults.json. Built for this region, NOT copied from Ghana: pumping energy is derived from water volume, head and pump efficiency; yields are FAOSTAT national means. Uncertainty is wide (factor ~2); every row carries a pedigree. Never invent fertiliser rates here.

provenance.span: Most cultivation is rain-fed; smallholders work by hand or animal traction (CIAT; BFS/USAID 2016, Senegal CSA profile). Screening 0 L diesel, 0 kWh.
Watering-can / bucket irrigation (Niayes market gardens) is human labour: no diesel or grid energy.
Motor-pump horticulture: 7000 m3/ha/season x 12 m head (well lift + hose pressure), small diesel pumpset overall efficiency 0.15: hydraulic 229 kWh / (0.15 x 10.75 kWh/L) = 142 L/ha.
Groundnut basin: animal-traction seeders and hoes dominate; partial mechanisation means occasional hired tractor ploughing or shelling. Screening 10 L/ha.
Senegal River Valley village rice scheme: diesel pump 15000 m3/ha x 4 m lift, efficiency 0.25 = 61 L/ha, plus ~35 L/ha hired land preparation.
Full tractor suite on light sandy (dior) soils: screening 50 L/ha within the mechanised-cereal band 40-80 L/ha; no default grid electricity.
Large Senegal River Valley schemes: electric pumping station 15000 m3/ha x 4 m, wire-to-water efficiency 0.6 = 272 kWh/ha; tractor + combine ~90 L/ha.

sources.note: Tier 1 activity-data approach; this table supplies activity amounts, not emission factors.
CIAT; BFS/USAID (2016) Climate-Smart Agriculture in Senegal: rainfed dominates; irrigated rice (SRV) and horticulture (Niayes) are the irrigated systems.

FAOSTAT (2025) Crops and livestock products (QCL), Yield (kg/ha), bulk Production_Crops_Livestock_E_Africa.csv dated 2025-12-23. Mean of 2021-2023; see the region's yield-guide file for flags and pedigree.

Pump energy = volume x 9.81 x head / 3.6e6 / efficiency (kWh); diesel L = hydraulic kWh / (efficiency x 10.75 kWh/L, 38.7 MJ/L). Efficiencies: small diesel pumpset 0.15, larger diesel 0.25, electric wire-to-water 0.6 (FAO Irrigation Water Management training manuals, pump efficiency ranges). Field-operation diesel uses the mechanised-cereal 40-80 L/ha band. Reviewer to confirm against national surveys.
